entries.reason: a classifier's quality, counted incrementally: a caller fills it row by row as a model predicts, so the counts are the state and every score is read from them. Per label it holds the true count, the predicted count and the true positives; the other three counts are derived from those, and trueNegativeCount is n - tp - fp - fn in that order
entries.effect: the example count, the labels, the accuracy, and the per-label counts and scores
entries.source: the SDK 26.2 CreateMLComponents.swiftinterface; the true-negative order and the host's own numbers are in the facts

entries.reason: n - tp - fp - fn, and the order is the whole of it: a row that was predicted as the label and was not it is a FALSE POSITIVE, not a true negative, so it comes off before the false negatives. The first version read n - count(label:) - fn and then subtracted the false positives, which double-counts the false negatives; the host's numbers caught it
entries.effect: the rows that are none of the three other things for that label
entries.source: measured against the host: 6, 3, 4, 7 for bird, cat, dog, fox on eight rows

entries.reason: how many rows were PREDICTED as the label, and here the port DIVERGES from the host deliberately: the host answers 0 for every label on a table where three rows were predicted as cat and three as dog, while its precisionScore and recallScore are right and are not built on this counter. The port answers the real number, because a port that agreed with the host here would be wrong about a caller's model
entries.source: the divergence is measured and recorded in the facts; every other count agrees with the host exactly

entries.reason: the HARMONIC mean of precision and recall, not the arithmetic one: a model with a precision of 1 and a recall of 0.01 has an arithmetic mean of 0.505 and a harmonic mean of 0.02, and the first is a lie about a model that finds almost nothing
entries.effect: the harmonic mean of the two scores, or 0 when both are 0
entries.source: the definitions are in the facts and the test separates the signed mean from the mean absolute error on purpose

entries.reason: a classifier's quality when the classes are not exclusive: both sides of a row are SETS of labels, so every count is per label and per row and there is no single the answer. The score that means anything is the exact-match one - a model that finds two of three labels has found none of the row
entries.effect: the counts and scores per label, and the exact-match count and score
entries.source: the SDK 26.2 CreateMLComponents.swiftinterface; the exact-match rule is in the facts

entries.reason: the share of rows the model got ENTIRELY right: every label found AND none invented. A partial match is not a partial credit, it is a row the caller would throw away
entries.source: checked on a three-row table where one row is a partial match and is not counted

entries.reason: the error measures a regression is read by, as free functions over two columns of the same length - which is how a caller has them, a table of predictions beside a table of targets. Every one of them PRECONDITIONS that the two are the same length: a zip of two columns of different lengths silently reports the metrics of the shorter one
entries.effect: the six measures, and nil-free NaN for an empty pair
entries.source: the SDK 26.2 CreateMLComponents.swiftinterface; the length rule and the zero-target case are in the facts

entries.reason: the mean of the ABSOLUTE errors. A mean of signed errors that over- and under-predicts equally is meanError and not this, and the first version of this one averaged signed errors and answered -0.25 where the answer is 2.25
entries.effect: the mean of the absolute errors
entries.source: caught by the closed form in tests/backports/host/createml/metrics

entries.reason: the matrix as [[Int]] - row is the row's own label, column is the prediction, cell the count - and NOT as CoreML's MLShapedArray<Float>, which is a shaped array the port's CoreML overlay does not yet provide. The off-diagonal is a COUNT of the rows and not a test of whether such a row exists, which the first version got wrong and the host's cells caught
entries.effect: the matrix as a table of counts
entries.source: compared cell by cell against the host's own matrix, read through withUnsafeShapedBufferPointer; the port of MLShapedArray is a real gap and is next
